reasoning:
**Question.** Yes if, after 16 November 2026 and before 1 January 2027, the holder of any of 24 top posts (President, Vice President, 15 department heads, EPA, OMB, DNI, CIA, USTR, SBA, White House chief of staff) leaves office or announces an exit dated before 1 January. Exits set for January, or waiting on a successor's confirmation, do not count. Susie Wiles's exit (6 November) came before the window.

**Starting point.** The question's own list of midterm losses gives two qualifying years of four; a wider count since 1982 gives about five of eleven (Bentsen 1994, O'Neill 2002, Rumsfeld 2006, Mattis 2018). This administration's 2026 pace agrees: five of these posts changed hands this year (Noem, Bondi, Chavez-DeRemer, Gabbard, Wiles), about 45% for the 38 days left at a steady rate.

**Recent evidence.**
- Nothing has qualified yet: Kalshi's "next Cabinet member out" market was still open on 22 November (Kalshi News). Politico (22 November) and MS NOW (23 November) report a stalled nominations backlog, 16 Senate days before Democrats take the chamber on 3 January, and no new Cabinet-level nominee.
- In a 60 Minutes interview released 6 November (CBS News), Trump promised "maybe a few changes" to his Cabinet, without names or timing.
- Most exposed: Commerce Secretary Lutnick (Nvidia export-control scandal; Trump on 20 November: "not lost confidence"; Senate testimony 10 December), Homeland Security Secretary Mullin (government-jet flap) and Defense Secretary Hegseth (Trump, 5 November: "every intention to keep him"). On 22 November markets priced an exit before 2027 near 20% for Lutnick, 10-11% for Hegseth, 10% for Mullin and 5-8% for several others. Such contracts run high (Hegseth was about 35% on 7 November), so I shade them.

**Combining.** The shaded chances sum to about 0.75 expected exits, and shake-ups cluster, leaving roughly even odds of at least one. Yes needs Trump to drop Lutnick around his testimony, a secretary to quit by year-end ahead of Democratic oversight, or a reshuffle under chief of staff Miller. No needs the White House to keep confirmed secretaries it could not replace through a Democratic Senate.

**Forecast: 50%.**
question_title: Will any of these high-ranking U.S. officials leave office before January 1, 2027?
